chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second [Imam al-Baqir] about the child, when is he considered to be in the state of Ihram? He (peace be upon him) said: When he can safeguard [himself, i.e., reach the age of discernment/maturity].

key_terms.اثَّغَرَ: He reached the age of discernment/maturity (lit. he was able to safeguard)
key_terms.يُحْرَمُ: He is put into Ihram / He enters the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: At what age or condition does a child enter Ihram for Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the obligation of Ihram for a child is triggered by 'ithghar' (reaching the age of discernment or maturity), rather than a fixed chronological age. This aligns with the Shia juristic principle that religious obligations (*taklif*) commence upon the attainment of mental and physical maturity, ensuring the child can comprehend and fulfill the rituals of Hajj. The term 'ithghar' is often interpreted by scholars as the point where a child gains sufficient understanding to distinguish right from wrong and manage their religious duties.
